message.content:
**The Thinker (Le Penseur) – Auguste Rodin (1880–1902)**  

Rodin’s bronze “The Thinker” is widely regarded as the most iconic sculpture of the 19th century. Though the final cast dates from 1902, the original concept was conceived in 1880 and first exhibited in 1887, firmly placing it in the late‑Victorian era. Its powerful, contemplative pose and the way it captures the human mind in motion have made it a cultural touchstone, inspiring countless reproductions, parodies, and scholarly discussions.  

Other contemporaneous masterpieces—such as Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889), “The Gates of Hell” (1880s), and Bartholdi’s “Statue of Liberty” (1886)—are also celebrated, but “The Thinker” remains the most frequently cited and reproduced sculpture from that century.
